sourceTitle: Ask HN: Any interesting books you have read lately?

books.title: The Aftermath
books.author: Philip Bump
books.reason: Demographic data connect cohort size, wealth and political power. Separating age, period and cohort effects is harder than the charts suggest; near-term American politics lowers durability. Clear journalism provides some institutional utility, but the national focus limits fit.

books.title: Lush Life
books.author: David Hajdu
books.reason: Collaboration, credit allocation and the constraints on artistic work provide a modest transferable payload. Researched musical biography supports evidence and prose more than causal modeling or strategic relevance; much of the value remains personal and cultural.

books.title: Fashion Climbing
books.author: Bill Cunningham
books.theme: New York fashion and celebrity milieu
books.reason: Observations on craft, client demand and finding a niche survive the personal story. Memoir limits independent verification and the causal account; readable recollections do not make this a useful model of industrial organization.

books.title: Kings of Their Own Ocean
books.author: Karen Pinchin
books.reason: Fish tagging, scarcity, pricing and international supply chains connect biology with commercial incentives. Reporting supplies a useful resource-governance case, but conservation is central and the narrative follows individual characters more than formal models.

books.title: Empire of the Summer Moon
books.author: S. C. Gwynne
books.reason: Horse mobility, raiding and changing military advantage retain practical mechanisms. The new thread adds enthusiasm and a reading list, not corroboration for broad ethnic characterizations. Those limits already justify the earlier low evidence and precision scores; all components remain.

books.title: Killers of the Flower Moon
books.author: David Grann
books.reason: Resource rents, guardianship and captured enforcement explain the crimes beyond individual villains. The thread corrects a film-title confusion but adds no new quality evidence. Research, clear structure and durable institutional lessons support the unchanged vector and non-veto decision.

books.title: Frontier Blood
books.author: Jo Ella Powell Exley
books.reason: Family networks, religious organization and frontier conflict offer limited institutional lessons. Contemporary accounts improve evidence, but the narrow family chronology constrains transfer, systems breadth and density for this reader.

books.title: Nine Years Among the Indians, 1870–1879
books.author: Herman Lehmann
books.reason: A mediated retrospective captivity account can illuminate adaptation, language and group membership. It is testimony rather than a reliable general model of indigenous societies; recall, editorial mediation and local detail keep evidence and utility modest.

books.title: The Heart of Everything That Is
books.author: Bob Drury; Tom Clavin
books.reason: Coalition formation, military asymmetry and negotiation give the biography some transfer. Reconstructed motives and a heroic narrative require caution; the thread's praise does not settle source reliability or its claims about Red Cloud's uniqueness.

books.title: Indigenous Continent
books.author: Pekka Hämäläinen
books.reason: Indigenous power, diplomacy and shifting territorial control challenge simple conquest narratives. Scholarly breadth earns authority; compression, contested interpretation and the thread's concrete complaints about transitions reduce evidence, density and structure. Evin Rias is a narrator, not a coauthor.

books.title: Ecology of the Planted Aquarium
books.author: Diana Walstad
books.reason: Nutrient cycles, chemical constraints and low-input system design give this aquarium manual real mechanistic value. It is unusually useful within its niche; transfer to other engineered systems is analogical and the dominant subject remains ecology.

books.title: Silent Spring
books.author: Rachel Carson
books.reason: Persistence, biological accumulation and unintended intervention effects provide lasting risk lessons. Historical reporting is not current toxicological guidance, but age alone does not invalidate a clearly historical work. The environmental focus warrants the deduction despite good evidence and prose.

books.title: Material World
books.author: Ed Conway
books.reason: Six material chains connect extraction, purification, process limits, capital and geopolitical dependence. Concrete production reporting gives exceptionally strong integration and fit. It is an explanatory synthesis rather than a quantified universal theory, so evidence and mechanisms stop below their maxima.

books.title: Lombard Street
books.author: Walter Bagehot
books.reason: Liquidity, confidence, reserves and lender-of-last-resort behavior form a compact reusable model. The nineteenth-century setting is explicit; it is not a description of today's banking system. Read its institutional details historically while keeping its durable crisis mechanisms.

books.title: The New Lombard Street
books.author: Perry Mehrling
books.reason: Funding liquidity, market liquidity and dealer balance sheets explain modern financial fragility. The money-market perspective bridges institutions and market mechanics with unusual density. The Federal Reserve is central, but the dollar system and strategic implications are global, so no American-only deduction applies.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.author: Richard Rhodes
books.reason: The new comments correctly emphasize links among science, industrial scale, military decisions and rival programs. They add no independent correction to the specialist evidence reviewed earlier. Every component remains justified; familiar physics and long biography still limit incremental density for this reader.

prior.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb

books.title: Energy: A Human History
books.author: Richard Rhodes
books.reason: Energy transitions join conversion efficiency, infrastructure, institutions and practical invention. Broad historical coverage creates useful comparisons but less depth on any one technology or economic model. The book's main purpose is energy development, so environmental passages do not trigger the deduction.

books.title: The Prize
books.author: Daniel Yergin
books.reason: Petroleum links geology, capital, production, transport and military power. The thread supplies a comparison with Rhodes, not new verification. Its integrated mechanisms still justify the prior vector; company-centered access and great length remain the main limits.

books.title: The Years of Lyndon Johnson (series)
books.author: Robert A. Caro
books.reason: The series makes information, procedure, appointments and money into mechanisms of power. The new comments reinforce readability, but repeat praise is not a quality bonus. Retain all earlier components and the deduction. The separately named Master of the Senate is also assessed; do not count it as independent validation.
books.identity: The four-volume series and the separately named Master of the Senate are distinct source units, not independent evidence for each other. No unnamed volumes are added as separate titles.

books.title: Twilight of the Bombs
books.author: Richard Rhodes
books.reason: Weapons verification, bargaining and institutions explain post-Cold-War proliferation decisions. Technical and political layers fit well; the policy endpoint is historical and the disarmament outlook needs independent scrutiny. Clear narrative earns its length better than a general policy manifesto.

books.title: Dreaming: A Very Short Introduction
books.author: J. Allan Hobson
books.reason: An expert presents physiological mechanisms and contrasts them with symbolic dream interpretation. Its compact scope is useful, but older hypotheses are not a current consensus review and direct strategic transfer is limited. Sleep itself is not automatically a disease theme.
books.identity: Originally Dreaming (2002); the Very Short Introduction edition is 2005. The source names the latter.

books.title: The Most Fun I Never Want to Have Again
books.author: R. D. Koncerak
books.reason: Bank formation, capitalization, credit risk and local market positioning supply practical mechanisms. Insider access helps, while one founder's retrospective account needs external checks. The regional US banking failure setting and institutional specificity warrant the thematic deduction and restrained evidence score.
books.identity: The author is R. D. Koncerak. This resolves a misleading initial title match.

books.title: Risk & Reward
books.author: Stephen Catlin; James Burcke
books.reason: Underwriting, pricing uncertainty, capital and portfolio exposure map directly to strategic risk. Practitioner access gives strong authority within insurance, with survivor and memoir bias limiting evidence. The international business focus prevents a national-history deduction.

books.title: Why Greatness Cannot Be Planned
books.author: Kenneth O. Stanley; Joel Lehman
books.reason: Novelty search and stepping-stone discovery offer a useful model of exploration when objectives mislead. Computational demonstrations support the mechanism better than sweeping claims about all institutions or life plans. Concise exposition transfers to research strategy without proving that planning generally fails.

books.title: A Game of Birds and Wolves
books.author: Simon Parkin
books.reason: Operational games, submarine tactics and feedback between analysis and combat form a strong case in modeling under uncertainty. Dramatic storytelling can overconcentrate credit, so evidence and authority are below specialist-monograph levels. The payload is military learning, not merely a roster of participants.

books.title: Detroit: I Do Mind Dying
books.author: Dan Georgakas; Marvin Surkin
books.theme: American urban and racial labor history
books.reason: Firsthand material on workplace organization and collective action supplies a real institutional payload. Advocacy and one city's industrial conflict limit generalization; the argument needs comparison with alternative accounts. Poor topic fit and political sympathy alone do not establish ideological capture.

books.title: Bullshit Jobs
books.author: David Graeber
books.reason: The taxonomy of perceived useless work and managerial incentives is thought-provoking. Self-selected testimony cannot measure prevalence or establish the economic necessity of the proposed categories. Retain the diagnostic questions with low confidence; a source's changed outlook is not causal evidence.

books.title: Thought as a System
books.author: David Bohm
books.reason: Treating thought and reaction as a feedback process can expose hidden assumptions in groups. Seminar dialogue and introspection do not validate a general psychological mechanism; Bohm's physics standing does not transfer automatically. Some practical reflective utility survives the repetition.

books.title: On Dialogue
books.author: David Bohm
books.reason: Suspending assumptions and listening for collective error give usable discussion heuristics. A short philosophical treatment is durable and clear, but lacks strong comparative evidence for organizational outcomes and offers limited systems or technical depth.

books.title: Invisible China
books.author: Scott Rozelle; Natalie Hell
books.reason: Rural education, health and labor-market change connect human capital to development constraints. Field research supports the diagnosis better than a deterministic middle-income-trap forecast. Cross-country comparisons aid transfer, but the book's predominant object remains China's national development.

books.title: The Power Broker
books.author: Robert A. Caro
books.reason: Control of authorities, finance and infrastructure explains power outside elected office. The HN endorsement adds no evidence that changes the prior allocation. Strong mechanisms and research survive, while extensive local detail and the urban-political subject retain their costs.

books.title: Boss
books.author: Mike Royko
books.reason: Patronage, service delivery and electoral control give a compact model of machine politics. Contemporary journalism supplies access but also a strong critical viewpoint. Local institutional lessons transfer partly; the political biography still has poor direct fit.

books.title: Master of the Senate
books.author: Robert A. Caro
books.reason: Rules, coalition management and procedural leverage remain the strongest payload. The new comment names this volume explicitly and praises its research, but supplies no independent quality check. Keep the prior full vector, length cost and American political deduction.

books.title: Capitalism and Desire
books.author: Todd McGowan
books.reason: A Lacanian interpretation of desire offers a lens on consumption and dissatisfaction. It does not identify economic causes through comparative tests; evidence, mechanisms and practical transfer therefore remain low. Philosophical interpretation is not automatically factual fraud or a veto based on political outlook.

books.title: Libidinal Economy
books.author: Jean-François Lyotard
books.reason: This difficult philosophical experiment supplies concepts about desire and social organization, not an empirical economic model. That interpretive payload prevents a confident no-payload veto, but weak operational definitions, low clarity and little direct application make it a very poor fit.

books.title: The Inner Citadel
books.author: Pierre Hadot
books.reason: Close reading reconstructs Stoic exercises and the logic behind Marcus Aurelius's notes. Scholarly care and durability are strong; repetition and limited institutional or technical reach reduce density and fit. This is disciplined intellectual history rather than generic motivational advice.

books.title: Two Years Before the Mast
books.author: Richard Henry Dana Jr.
books.reason: Shipboard labor, trade logistics and hierarchical discipline give the eyewitness account more than local color. Retrospective memoir and limited causal analysis constrain transfer. The California coastal economy and social setting predominate despite the ocean voyage.

books.title: The Captured Economy
books.author: Brink Lindsey; Steven M. Teles
books.reason: Finance, intellectual property, occupational licensing and land use show how rules create rents. Policy comparisons give strong institutional utility; causal magnitude and alternative reforms remain contested. American policy is the main object and influence, requiring the deduction.

books.title: Tyranny, Inc.
books.author: Sohrab Ahmari
books.reason: Cases of private coercion expose bargaining power and weak exit options. The broad policy remedy is less securely established than the harms described, lowering evidence and transfer. Political advocacy alone is not a serious V2 finding; retain with low confidence and a domestic-policy deduction.

books.title: American Revolutions
books.author: Alan Taylor
books.reason: Imperial competition, war, land and institutional formation explain revolution beyond founder biography. Scholarly scope and evidence are strong, but long national origins history has low direct fit. Mechanisms preserve eligibility despite the explicit thematic cost.

books.title: The Mind Illuminated
books.author: John Yates; Matthew Immergut; Jeremy Graves
books.reason: A detailed staged practice supplies attention-training procedures. The claimed neuroscience and progression should not be treated as validated clinical mechanisms; length and specialized spiritual aims lower density and fit. Meditation is not itself a listed thematic deduction or a veto.

books.title: The Attention Revolution
books.author: B. Alan Wallace
books.reason: The graded concentration exercises offer a transferable practice framework. The source's claim that this is nonspiritual is too strong: Buddhist commitments matter to the account. Practical instructions remain separable from metaphysical claims, so score conservatively rather than veto by affiliation.

books.title: The Practicing Stoic
books.author: Ward Farnsworth
books.reason: Thematic organization of Stoic arguments gives compact tools for judgment, control and response to setbacks. Textual clarity and durability are stronger than empirical or systems depth. Useful reflective philosophy, but limited incremental value for the requested industrial-strategic profile.

books.title: Goodbye to a River
books.author: John Graves
books.reason: The river journey chiefly preserves local stories, landscape and personal memory. After removing that setting, too little developed mechanism remains for this reading purpose. Literary quality and historical testimony retain counterfactual points; the rejection is a low-transfer judgment, not a claim of falsehood.

books.title: The WEIRDest People in the World
books.author: Joseph Henrich
books.reason: Kinship, church rules and psychology remain a serious comparative hypothesis. The thread's dating-app and polygamy speculation is not the book's demonstrated result. Historical identification and alternative explanations remain the binding limits, so every prior component and low confidence stay unchanged.

prior.title: The WEIRDest People in the World

books.title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
books.author: Robert M. Pirsig
books.reason: Pirsig's account mixes a real journey, altered narrative and philosophical argument. His author's note asserts a factual essence; the publisher explicitly discusses its ambiguous fact-fiction boundary. Retain conditionally as philosophical autobiography. Attention, diagnosis and quality supply transferable craft heuristics, while an elusive central concept and long personal narrative limit precision and density.
books.identity: Genre is conditional: philosophical autobiography with altered narrative, rather than an established wholly fictional novel. The hard exclusion is not applied merely because some catalogues call it a novel.

books.title: Shadow Divers
books.author: Robert Kurson
books.reason: Equipment constraints, uncertain identification and error correction remain the useful payload. The new interest prompted by a submersible accident is a reading trigger, not evidence. Retain the previous score vector; this is a technical investigation with international historical significance.

books.title: Breath
books.author: James Nestor
books.reason: The source offers self-reported improvement, not controlled validation of broad health claims. The earlier evidence, authority and precision limits remain appropriate, while basic physiology and habit awareness prevent a no-payload veto. No newly verified central defect establishes a firmer whole-book gate.

books.title: Generations
books.author: Jean M. Twenge
books.reason: Large datasets make generational comparison concrete. Age, period and cohort are confounded, and attributing shifts to technology requires more than parallel trends. It is a useful descriptive resource with limited causal certainty and predominantly American relevance.

books.title: The Chip
books.author: T. R. Reid
books.reason: Device invention, manufacturing and entrepreneurial organization explain the integrated circuit's practical leverage. Its compact history fits well, although it is less global and less current than Chip War. The source's claimed endpoint in the US-China chip conflict is not established for Reid's older edition.
books.identity: First publication 1984; the linked revised edition is 2001. The comment’s claimed US–China endpoint is not established for this book.

books.title: Chip War
books.author: Chris Miller
books.reason: Fabrication constraints, industrial specialization, supply networks and strategic dependence form a strong integrated explanation. The account has broad historical reach but remains a narrative synthesis with selective coverage. Its 2022 policy endpoint does not diminish the durable production mechanisms.

books.title: The Primacy of Doubt
books.author: Tim Palmer
books.reason: Ensemble prediction, chaotic dynamics and probabilistic decisions fit the reader's interests. Familiar physics lowers novelty; the proposed extensions to quantum foundations need to remain distinct from established weather-prediction practice. The organizing subject is uncertainty across domains, not predominantly ecology.

books.title: The Tao of Wu
books.author: RZA
books.reason: Creative discipline and personal resilience offer modest heuristics, but autobiographical and spiritual claims are not tested explanations. Compact recollections preserve some readability; celebrity-centered context and low technical or institutional transfer make this a poor fit.

books.title: American Prometheus
books.author: Kai Bird; Martin J. Sherwin
books.reason: The new thread emphasizes personal relationships rather than new scientific evidence. The research organization, security institutions and globally consequential weapons work still support the scientific-biography exception and prior vector. The title's word tragedy alone does not define a predominantly American-tragedy topic.

books.title: Double Cross
books.author: Ben Macintyre
books.reason: Deception requires managing channels, credibility, feedback and adversary expectations. Archival narrative gives strong strategic examples, although reconstructed intentions and successful-case selection limit general rules. The personalities serve an international operational problem rather than isolated biography.

books.title: The Splendid and the Vile
books.author: Erik Larson
books.reason: Leadership, morale and communication under bombardment offer some transferable lessons. The domestic and personal focus gives less operational depth than its wartime setting may suggest. Readable archival narrative survives the required political-figure deduction.

books.title: The Second World War
books.author: Antony Beevor
books.reason: A global military synthesis links theaters, operational choices and civilian consequences. Broad integration and scholarly experience are strong, while immense coverage limits depth and reading efficiency. It is a comparative world-war account, not single-country history.

books.title: SAS: Rogue Heroes
books.author: Ben Macintyre
books.reason: Selection, initiative, unconventional operations and organizational resistance supply military lessons. Authorized archive access aids evidence but does not remove heroic narrative or institutional bias. Distinguish operational mechanisms from the thread's unverified suspicion of exaggeration.

books.title: 50 Years of Text Games
books.author: Aaron A. Reed
books.reason: One game per year traces changing interfaces, tools, communities and design constraints. It explains a technical culture with substantial documentary effort; long case-by-case coverage costs density for someone seeking broad strategy. History about fiction remains nonfiction.

books.title: Never Split the Difference
books.author: Chris Voss; Tahl Raz
books.reason: The thread supplies specific objections about salesmanship, anecdotal success and padding alongside practical examples of calibrated questions. Keep the reusable negotiation tools, but lower E by 1 and D by 2 from source 5. These objections justify caution, not a proven wholesale fabrication veto.

books.title: Getting to Yes
books.author: Roger Fisher; William Ury; Bruce Patton
books.reason: Interests, outside options and separating people from the bargaining problem form durable reusable heuristics. Research and practice support authority, but cooperative framing is not a full model of coercive or asymmetric negotiations. Concise architecture makes the method easy to use.

books.title: The Genius of the Few
books.author: Christian O'Brien; Barbara Joy O'Brien
books.reason: The reconstruction treats contested readings of myth as evidence for an actual civilizing group and Garden of Eden history. The project's own research proposal still seeks archaeological substantiation. The central historical inference is not established; entertainment and speculative coherence cannot replace evidence.

books.title: The 12th Planet
books.author: Zecharia Sitchin
books.reason: The ancient-astronaut account depends on mistranslated Mesopotamian terms and unsupported astronomical readings. Heiser's source-based examination directly challenges the Nibiru foundation. These are central evidence failures, not merely speculative details around a sound historical explanation.

books.title: The Earth Chronicles
books.author: Zecharia Sitchin
books.reason: The nominated series extends the same ancient-astronaut reconstruction. Its underlying textual and astronomical bridge remains unsupported, and repeating the premise through several volumes adds no independent evidence. The long series also loses density relative to the already weak first-volume case.
books.identity: Series-level assessment of the seven main Earth Chronicles volumes; no average reader rating is assigned across the set.

books.title: The Anunnaki Chronicles
books.author: Zecharia Sitchin; Janet Sitchin, editor
books.reason: This edited collection documents Sitchin's research history but does not repair the mistranslations and unsupported ancient-astronaut premise. Archival access to an author's notes earns limited documentary credit, not validation of the central historical explanation.

books.title: Blue Ocean Strategy
books.author: W. Chan Kim; Renée Mauborgne
books.reason: Value curves and shifting competitive dimensions are useful strategy tools. Retrospectively selected success cases do not show that firms can systematically create uncontested markets; lower evidence and precision accordingly. The framework has lasting use beyond the marketing terminology.

books.title: Too Perfect
books.author: Allan E. Mallinger; Jeannette DeWyze
books.reason: Clinical patterns and practical exercises can help readers identify costly control habits. Case narratives are weak evidence for general treatment effects, and direct domain fit is minimal. The psychological-disorder focus warrants the thematic cost without implying a categorical veto of therapy books.

books.title: The E-Myth Revisited
books.author: Michael E. Gerber
books.reason: Separating technical work from running a repeatable business exposes process and delegation constraints. The franchise model is not universally optimal and case-based advice limits evidence. Revisited is the 1995 revision; the thread's 1985 date belongs to the original E-Myth.
books.identity: 1995 is the revised work. Goodreads merges some 1985 metadata from the original E-Myth; that date is not used for this title.

books.title: Outlive
books.author: Peter Attia; Bill Gifford
books.reason: Risk factors, prevention and exercise connect several physiological and decision layers. Established findings coexist with extrapolated screening and longevity prescriptions; the source's personal response does not validate them. Substantial length and disease-centered content lower priority; no whole-book veto is asserted from this check.

books.title: Four Thousand Weeks
books.author: Oliver Burkeman
books.reason: Finite time, opportunity costs and impossible completion provide durable planning heuristics. The argument is reflective rather than experimentally validated and has little institutional or technical depth. Its brevity and clear structure preserve some utility despite the self-help focus.

books.title: The Good Virus
books.author: Tom Ireland
books.reason: Phage-host mechanisms, experimental history and treatment development connect science with practical constraints. The comment's claim of inevitable clinical integration is stronger than the evidence warrants and is not adopted. Disease treatment predominates despite the interesting molecular science.

books.title: Stop Reading the News
books.author: Rolf Dobelli
books.reason: Attention budgets and selection costs give a reusable idea, but categorical news avoidance is not a demonstrated optimum for strategic understanding. Broad prescriptions outpace the evidence. Short exposition earns density, with low direct fit and limited causal development.

books.title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
books.author: Mark Manson
books.reason: Choosing commitments and accepting constraints provide a small practical payload. Anecdotes, repetition and rhetorical certainty carry more weight than testable mechanisms. The book remains included because dislike of self-help is not an additional exclusion rule.

books.title: Turning the Mind into an Ally
books.author: Sakyong Mipham
books.reason: Attention practice and noticing reactions offer reusable exercises. Buddhist framing and personal teaching experience do not establish empirical efficacy or a general cognitive model. The practical portions prevent a categorical veto, but domain fit and systems depth are very low.

books.title: Why Calories Don't Count
books.author: Giles Yeo
books.reason: Digestion, absorption and measurement limitations explain why nominal calorie labels are imperfect proxies. The title does not repeal energy conservation. Expert authority and mechanisms are good, while the weight-loss and obesity focus limits personal priority.

books.title: All That the Rain Promises and More
books.author: David Arora
books.reason: A compact identification reference offers explicit discrimination procedures and practical observational skills. It is dense and authoritative within its purpose, but has little strategic or technical transfer for this reader. Species identification is not automatically environmental advocacy or ecology predominance.

books.title: The Big Con
books.author: Mariana Mazzucato; Rosie Collington
books.reason: Outsourcing, information asymmetry and loss of institutional capability form useful mechanisms. The book's broad indictment needs clearer counterfactuals and comparison with beneficial consulting. Cross-national business and state-capacity relevance prevents an automatic American-theme deduction.

books.title: Adult Children of Emotionally Immature Parents
books.author: Lindsay C. Gibson
books.reason: Recognizing patterns and setting interpersonal limits supplies modest transfer. Clinical stories and broad parent categories do not establish a validated causal taxonomy. The thread shows perceived usefulness, not clinical verification; direct domain fit is negligible, but no serious veto is established.

books.title: Codependent No More
books.author: Melody Beattie
books.reason: Boundary setting and distinguishing help from control remain usable ideas. A broad codependency label, dated examples and spiritual recovery framing limit evidence and precision. The thread itself supplies these qualifications. Religion and self-help are not automatic thematic deductions.

books.title: The Defining Decade
books.author: Meg Jay
books.reason: Skill accumulation, relationships and timing provide a practical framework for early adulthood. Clinical anecdotes and cohort generalizations overstate a uniform life schedule; little addresses the reader's core domains. Preserve limited usefulness without treating age-based urgency as a proven law.

books.title: Set Boundaries, Find Peace
books.author: Nedra Glover Tawwab
books.reason: Concrete communication and boundary procedures have practical interpersonal value. The empirical base and causal model are limited, and business or scientific transfer is indirect. Clear, accessible structure earns points while the topic remains a poor match.

books.title: No More Mr. Nice Guy
books.author: Robert A. Glover
books.reason: The thread identifies unsupported gendered origin stories and substantial filler while describing usable boundary and covert-contract ideas. Lower E by 2 and D by 1 from source 5. The practical payload remains, so a serious whole-book V1 or V2 gate is not proven here.

books.title: Love and Limerence
books.author: Dorothy Tennov
books.reason: Interview-based description gives a useful vocabulary for intrusive romantic attachment. Sampling and retrospective reports limit causal conclusions; naming a pattern does not establish a universal disorder or treatment. Durable descriptive psychology has very low direct domain fit.

books.title: When I Say No, I Feel Guilty
books.author: Manuel J. Smith
books.reason: Assertive response patterns provide specific reusable scripts. Clinical experience supports limited authority, while dated social assumptions and thin comparative validation constrain evidence. There is a practical payload, although the reading priority is low for the stated interests.

books.title: The Golden Ass of Apuleius: The Liberation of the Feminine in Man
books.author: Marie-Louise von Franz
books.reason: This is von Franz's interpretive study, not Apuleius's novel. Archetypal reading supplies a literary lens, but should not be treated as a tested psychological decoder of one's childhood writing. Interpretive value prevents a confident no-payload veto; empirical and strategic scores remain low.
books.identity: The 1970 precursor is A Psychological Interpretation of The Golden Ass of Apuleius. The linked revised title is a later edition. This is nonfiction about a novel, not the novel itself.

books.title: Why We Get Fat
books.author: Gary Taubes
books.reason: The strong carbohydrate-insulin account makes causal claims that controlled metabolic studies do not support in the required form. This central inferential problem warrants V1, while readability and some physiological discussion retain counterfactual credit. This does not imply that carbohydrate restriction can never help an individual.

books.title: How Not to Die
books.author: Michael Greger; Gene Stone
books.reason: Food-pattern comparisons and prevention mechanisms offer some information, but selected studies and sweeping prevention or reversal language warrant caution about causality and generality. The source notes poor length efficiency. Retain provisionally; this check does not establish a precise whole-book fatal flaw.

books.title: The Dictator's Handbook
books.author: Bruce Bueno de Mesquita; Alastair Smith
books.reason: Coalition size, resource distribution and survival incentives give a clear reusable political model. One selectorate framework cannot explain every institution or motive, so evidence and precision are bounded. Evaluate explanatory utility without turning it into a guide to manipulative political conduct.

books.title: Why Nations Fail
books.author: Daron Acemoglu; James A. Robinson
books.reason: Institutional incentives, extraction and creative destruction connect prosperity with political constraints. Comparative cases support a useful framework but do not uniquely identify institutions against all rival causal accounts. Repetition and binary labels cost density and precision; profile-example status adds no bonus.

books.title: The Invention of Power
books.author: Bruce Bueno de Mesquita
books.reason: Bargaining between church and rulers proposes an institutional mechanism for European development. The bridge from medieval selection rules to long-run prosperity is ambitious and needs comparative validation. Retain as a hypothesis with low confidence rather than treating a sweeping explanation as established history.

books.title: The Dawn of Everything
books.author: David Graeber; David Wengrow
books.reason: The thread presents specific concerns about evidence selection, repetition and confident reconstruction, alongside defenses. Comparative social possibilities remain useful, but lower E, D and P by one each from source 6. Criticism alone does not establish that the whole comparative argument fails V1 or depends on allegiance under V2.

books.title: Sapiens
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.reason: The replies retract the claim that Dawn refutes most of Sapiens and identify an agricultural-transition argument that Sapiens partly already recognizes. No new verified decisive defect emerges. Keep the earlier low-confidence vector: memorable synthesis, limited causal identification and overconfident generalization.

books.title: The Dragons of Eden
books.author: Carl Sagan
books.reason: Evolution, cognition and speculative links among them give a compact history of ideas. The older brain models need historical framing; the book is explicitly speculative rather than current neuroscience. It does not become authoritative anthropology merely because a commenter prefers it to Sapiens.

books.title: Mein Kampf
books.author: Adolf Hitler
books.theme: Political figure, racial ideology and national agenda
books.reason: Racial hierarchy, conspiracy and political allegiance organize the work and displace evidence. These are central ideological and epistemic failures. Its importance as a primary document about Nazism does not make its argument a reliable explanatory model; the historical-document use is distinct.

books.title: Saloons of the Old West
books.author: Richard Erdoes
books.reason: Local gathering places coordinate exchange, information and social order, which gives modest institutional transfer. Anecdotes dominate over systematic comparisons, and the American-West setting greatly limits direct fit. The thread's comparison with Hamblin is a reading device, not independent corroboration.

books.title: Jacob Hamblin: The Peacemaker
books.author: Pearson H. Corbett
books.theme: American frontier, religious leader and racial history
books.reason: Settlement networks, cross-cultural mediation and religious authority provide some mechanisms. A sympathetic religious biography and miracle reports require source criticism; the thread explicitly flags that framing. Retain low-confidence historical material without endorsing supernatural claims or assuming all testimony is worthless.

books.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
books.author: Jared Diamond
books.reason: The thread links to substantive historian objections, reinforcing rather than newly resolving the limits already recorded. Domestication, diffusion and material constraints retain explanatory value; cultural autonomy and case-specific conquest need other evidence. Keep all earlier points and provisional non-veto status, not a claim of specialist consensus.

books.title: Masters of Doom
books.author: David Kushner
books.reason: Engine limits, iteration speed, business choices and team conflict provide a useful account of software production. Reporting and memorable structure are strong, but reconstructed scenes and a narrow successful company limit inference. Romero's later memoir is a comparison source, not automatic proof that either account is correct.

books.title: Doom Guy: Life in First Person
books.author: John Romero
books.reason: A participant describes design, production and team decisions from inside id Software. Direct access earns authority, while selective memory and self-presentation lower evidence. The scientific and technical memoir exception applies; the personal detail gives less density than the best systems histories.

books.title: Impro
books.author: Keith Johnstone
books.reason: Status behavior, inhibition and spontaneous cooperation yield reusable group-interaction heuristics. Exercises provide practical grounding, though they are not controlled social-science tests. Theatrical context lowers direct fit without removing the transferable payload or durable clarity.

books.title: Losing the Signal
books.author: Jacquie McNish; Sean Silcoff
books.reason: Engineering constraints, carrier relationships, product architecture and organizational incentives explain strategic failure. Reporting provides strong cross-layer lessons, while hindsight and access-dependent interpretation limit certainty. It is a technology-industry case with global consequences, not Canadian national history.

books.title: The Ark Before Noah
books.author: Irving Finkel
books.reason: Textual decipherment and a physical construction problem show how evidence constrains historical reconstruction. Specialist authority is strong; much of the payoff remains philological rather than strategic. Analysis of a myth is nonfiction and does not depend on the myth being literally true.

books.title: A Very English Scandal
books.author: John Preston
books.reason: Elite protection, reputational incentives and institutional discretion provide some transfer beyond the scandal. Reconstructed scenes and a tightly personal case constrain causal depth. Its political-figure focus receives the deduction even though the narrative is clear and durable.

books.title: The Theoretical Minimum
books.author: Leonard Susskind and collaborators
books.reason: The series teaches mathematical structure rather than avoiding equations. Accuracy and authority are strong, but an expert in QFT and cosmology will know most of the foundations. Treat the unnamed volumes as one nominated series; do not substitute the first volume's reader rating for a series aggregate.
books.identity: The source refers to Susskind’s accompanying book series without specifying a volume; the series is retained once and has no aggregate star rating.

books.title: How We Think
books.author: John Dewey
books.reason: Problem formulation, observation, inference and reflective testing form a durable account of inquiry. The philosophical and educational framework is stronger than any modern experimental validation. Concise conceptual discipline supports utility even though many examples predate contemporary science and organizations.

books.title: The Creative Act
books.author: Rick Rubin
books.reason: Attention, revision and willingness to experiment provide some creative heuristics. Aphorisms and intuition receive too much evidential weight; the thread's concern about a diagnosis anecdote reinforces that limit. Its subject is creative practice rather than the author's celebrity life, so no celebrity deduction is automatic.

books.title: The Matter with Things
books.author: Iain McGilchrist
books.reason: The move from hemispheric attention differences to a privileged account of reality exceeds what the neuroscience can establish. A favorable psychiatric review and Ellis's detailed objections show genuine disagreement; the central inferential bridge warrants V1 at moderate confidence, not rejection of every neurological observation.

books.title: The Master and His Emissary
books.author: Iain McGilchrist
books.reason: Corballis directly challenges the extension from brain asymmetry to Western cultural history. The new comments add repetition and scope concerns but no empirical repair. Retain the earlier gate and complete counterfactual vector, while acknowledging favorable specialist reception and real hemispheric asymmetries.

books.title: Prisoners of Geography
books.author: Tim Marshall
books.reason: Geography, transport routes and defensible borders provide useful constraints. Turning them into seemingly inevitable national behavior hides institutional choices and contingency, reducing evidence and precision. The source's 2017 date is a later edition, not the work's 2015 first publication.

books.title: Up in the Old Hotel
books.author: Joseph Mitchell
books.reason: The collection's strength is observation of particular New Yorkers and places. Little developed general mechanism remains after those portraits are removed, so V3 applies for this task. Literary control and documentary value still earn counterfactual credit; low fit alone is not the stated gate.

books.title: The Roman Empire in Crisis
books.author: Paul N. Pearson
books.reason: Military succession, border pressure and fragmented evidence can illuminate institutional fragility. New archaeological and textual material supports the narrow reconstruction, though causal reach is limited. Rome is a multi-region imperial system; this is not automatically modern single-nation history.

books.title: A Calendar of Wisdom
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.reason: A curated collection of ethical reflections offers prompts for judgment rather than a causal model. Source selection, mixed traditions and repetition limit coherence and evidence. The daily format and durable ideas supply modest utility, with almost no direct technical or institutional fit.

books.title: Proving Ground
books.author: Kathy Kleiman
books.reason: Recovering ENIAC programmers' work explains implementation labor, credit and knowledge loss. Oral testimony needs comparison with contemporary records, but the technical biography exception clearly applies. Women's participation is not a reason for an automatic minority-topic deduction; computing history is the central subject.

books.title: Pioneer Programmer
books.author: Jean Jennings Bartik
books.reason: Firsthand recollection preserves early programming practice and the organization of technical work. The source explicitly notes limited technical detail, so mechanism and density are restrained. Memoir bias lowers evidence, while the computing-biography exception supports eligibility.

books.title: Six Faces of Globalization
books.author: Anthea Roberts; Nicolas Lamp
books.reason: Contrasting six accounts of globalization makes tradeoffs, constituencies and hidden assumptions explicit. The comparative structure helps strategic reasoning across political frames. It maps competing causal stories more than it proves one complete model, keeping mechanism below the highest band.

books.title: How the World Thinks
books.author: Julian Baggini
books.reason: Cross-cultural comparison exposes assumptions about self, knowledge and institutions. Broad surveys necessarily compress disagreements within each tradition, limiting causal and evidential depth. Accessible structure and durable conceptual comparisons survive despite modest direct domain fit.

books.title: Art & Fear
books.author: David Bayles; Ted Orland
books.reason: Feedback, repetition and the cost of waiting for inspiration yield useful craft heuristics. Working artists provide practical authority but not strong causal evidence. A compact treatment earns density; low systems breadth and technical relevance keep it below the leading choices.

books.title: The Machine That Changed the World
books.author: James P. Womack; Daniel T. Jones; Daniel Roos
books.reason: Production flow, quality, supplier relationships and organizational design connect factory mechanics with competitive advantage. Comparative industrial research gives strong evidence and authority; retrospective success narratives still require limits. Manufacturing mechanisms remain useful even as specific industry rankings change.

books.title: Ultralearning
books.author: Scott H. Young
books.reason: Retrieval, feedback, direct practice and targeted drills provide reusable learning tools. Selected extreme learners do not establish a universal accelerated-learning recipe. The thread's mixed experiences reinforce limits on generality; familiar advice and anecdotal padding restrain density.

books.title: The Silk Roads
books.author: Peter Frankopan
books.reason: Trade corridors, empires, religion and resource competition give a useful shift in geographical perspective. The large synthesis sometimes turns selection into an organizing master narrative; evidence and precision are below specialist levels. Strong integration survives the length cost.

books.title: The Case for God
books.author: Karen Armstrong
books.reason: Distinguishing religious practice, symbolism and literal propositions can clarify conceptual disputes. The historical synthesis favors an interpretation of religion and needs counterexamples. A normative religious argument is not automatically ideological capture, but limited causal and strategic utility keeps priority low.

books.title: Nudge
books.author: Richard H. Thaler; Cass R. Sunstein
books.reason: Defaults, friction and presentation remain useful design mechanisms. Prior evidence includes small real-world effects and publication-bias concerns; neither universal success nor universal failure follows. Retain 68 and the non-veto gate. Source 8 names the original work, not specifically the 2021 Final Edition.
books.identity: The source names Nudge, not The Final Edition. The existing 2021 purchase link is retained as a revised edition; the original work is dated 2008. Do not create a duplicate title.

books.title: The Power of Habit
books.author: Charles Duhigg
books.reason: Cue-response-reward framing can help diagnose repeated behavior. The move from individual habits to civil-rights or organizational outcomes is less securely causal; the thread specifically identifies this drift and padding. Useful mechanisms remain, but no generic habit loop explains every social result.

books.title: The Design Thinking Playbook
books.author: Michael Lewrick; Patrick Link; Larry Leifer
books.reason: Problem framing, prototypes and feedback supply concrete product-work tools. Checklist breadth and business terminology substitute for stronger evidence about when each method works. It has practical transfer across teams, while fashion-sensitive framing and uneven density reduce priority.

books.title: Global Strategy
books.author: Mike W. Peng
books.reason: Industry, resources and institutions give a structured framework for cross-border strategy. Scholarly synthesis and varied cases support authority, but textbook breadth and dated examples cost density. Assess the named work without assuming the exact edition used by the commenter.
books.identity: Early release records give 2005; copyright and bibliographic records also give 2006. The linked textbook edition may be later.

books.title: Global Business
books.author: Mike W. Peng
books.reason: Institutions, markets and firm capabilities connect international business decisions. The comment explicitly says Global Business after Global Strategy, but may have switched titles accidentally; keep this second work conditionally identified. Textbook scope supports integration more than concentrated strategic depth.
books.identity: The same comment switches from Global Strategy to Global Business. It may mean Peng’s separate textbook or be a slip. This second entry is conditional; 2008 release/2009 copyright records differ.

books.title: Beautiful Country
books.author: Qian Julie Wang
books.reason: Migration status, incentives and access to institutions supply limited social mechanisms within a childhood memoir. Personal testimony is valuable but not a general causal study. The dominant American immigrant and minority experience receives the thematic deduction; concrete institutional constraints prevent V3.

books.title: The Code Book
books.author: Simon Singh
books.reason: Attacks, code design and information asymmetry make cryptography historically concrete. Technical examples are clear, but much will be familiar to a computational physicist and the book is not a current security manual. The comment's all-encompassing list of modern algorithms is not treated as a verified contents list.

books.title: Fermat's Last Theorem
books.author: Simon Singh
books.reason: The mathematical problem and proof culture show long-term research, collaboration and error correction. It explains context rather than the proof's full machinery, limiting technical novelty and strategic transfer. Scientific biography and accurate exposition keep it eligible and durable.

books.title: Almost Perfect
books.author: W. E. Pete Peterson
books.reason: Product decisions, sales, support and organizational dynamics provide lessons in software commercialization. A senior participant has exceptional access but a partial viewpoint; the author notes corrections to the online text. Use the free authorized version as an evidence source, not proof of neutral attribution.
books.identity: The author’s site dates publication to 1994; copyright and contemporary records also point to 1993. Both are shown; unrelated novels called Almost Perfect are rejected.

books.title: An Illustrated Book of Bad Arguments
books.author: Ali Almossawi
books.reason: Concise examples help identify invalid argument forms. Naming a fallacy does not decide an empirical dispute and the treatment cannot replace probabilistic reasoning. High density and clear organization are strengths; technical and institutional depth are limited.

books.title: Embracing Defeat
books.author: John W. Dower
books.reason: Occupation, legitimacy, reform and adaptation show how institutions change after military defeat. Research and systems connections are strong, while thick social detail lowers efficiency. The history's primary object is Japan's national reconstruction, so the deduction applies despite transferable lessons.

books.title: Sovietistan
books.author: Erika Fatland
books.reason: Travel across several post-Soviet states exposes institutional legacies, borders and resource dependence. Interview access and observation help, but snapshots and anecdotal selection limit causal confidence. Multiple countries and comparative regional influence prevent a single-nation deduction.

books.title: The Border
books.author: Erika Fatland
books.reason: Border encounters illuminate asymmetry, historical memory and relationships with a regional power. The many-country structure provides comparison, but travel observations are not controlled evidence. Its main unit is Russia's relations with neighbors rather than isolated national chronology.

books.title: A Thousand Plateaus
books.author: Gilles Deleuze; Félix Guattari
books.reason: Concepts of networks, multiplicity and organization offer interpretive possibilities. Loose cross-domain analogies and difficult prose provide little operational guidance or testable causal structure. Philosophical influence earns authority and durability, not empirical validation; low utility is not confidently zero payload.

books.title: When McKinsey Comes to Town
books.author: Walt Bogdanich; Michael Forsythe
books.reason: Conflicts of interest, institutional dependence and private advice connect business with public power. Investigative cases support the account of harms, but do not alone estimate net consulting value. International cases and general agency problems preserve broad fit beyond American corporate biography.

books.title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
books.author: James F. Kurose; Keith W. Ross
books.reason: Layering, congestion, reliability and security explain operational networks through explicit models and exercises. Strong technical authority and transfer justify priority, although textbook length and familiarity reduce density. Assess the established eighth-edition material, not a claim that every protocol detail is timeless.

books.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
books.author: Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau; Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau
books.reason: Virtualization, concurrency and persistence expose tradeoffs, invariants and failure modes. Public chapters, exercises and implementations make the reasoning checkable. Excellent technical fit is balanced by relatively narrow economic or institutional integration and some material already known to an experienced programmer.
books.identity: Early online versions precede the 2018 print edition. A later print identifier does not make 2018 the beginning of the online work.

books.title: Make It Stick
books.author: Peter C. Brown; Henry L. Roediger III; Mark A. McDaniel
books.reason: Retrieval, spacing and interleaving connect experimental learning research to usable practice. Transfer to complex expertise needs limits, but the evidence base is stronger than anecdotal accelerated-learning stories. Clear structure and moderate length support practical value.

books.title: God, Human, Animal, Machine
books.author: Meghan O'Gieblyn
books.reason: Tracing metaphors between theology and computing can reveal assumptions hidden in AI debates. This is an essayistic philosophical inquiry, not a technical theory of consciousness. Conceptual integration and prose are stronger than empirical mechanisms; its reflective payload prevents a religion-based veto.

books.title: The Body Keeps the Score
books.author: Bessel van der Kolk
books.reason: The new personal recommendation does not resolve the causal and treatment overreach examined in prior analyses. The published critical commentary supports retaining V1 at moderate confidence, not a field-wide unanimous verdict. Every counterfactual component and the disease deduction remain unchanged.

books.title: My Grandmother's Hands
books.author: Resmaa Menakem
books.reason: Somatic exercises and attention to learned reactions offer limited practical ideas. Biological and intergenerational explanations require stronger evidence than therapeutic anecdotes provide. Keep low-confidence inclusion rather than infer a decisive whole-book error from its association with other trauma books.

books.title: Killer in the Kremlin
books.author: John Sweeney
books.reason: Coercion, patronage and treatment of opponents give some institutional payload. A strongly personal prosecutorial narrative and news-linked scope constrain balance, durability and causal depth. Political biography warrants the deduction, without assuming that criticism of a ruler is ideological capture.

books.title: Open Borders
books.author: Bryan Caplan; Zach Weinersmith
books.reason: Migration, productivity, incentives and ethical tradeoffs form a clear argument with transferable economic content. Estimates of large gains depend on institutions and adjustment assumptions. Graphic nonfiction is eligible; immigration policy alone is not a listed thematic deduction.

books.title: Fungi of Temperate Europe
books.author: Thomas Læssøe; Jens H. Petersen
books.reason: A comprehensive visual reference supplies explicit identification structures and unusual taxonomic depth. It is strong within mycology but offers little transfer to the requested strategic domains. Length is justified as a reference; natural-history identification alone does not make ecology the predominant topic.

books.title: Truman
books.author: David McCullough
books.reason: Presidential decisions connect nuclear weapons, alliances and institutions, giving some general strategic lessons. An admiring, long biography is less efficient than a focused causal study. National politics and the political figure remain the main subject despite global consequences.

books.title: The End of the World Is Just the Beginning
books.author: Peter Zeihan
books.reason: Demography, energy and supply chains are relevant inputs, but the central value proposition is a confident forecast of broad deglobalization and unavoidable collapse. Scenario possibilities are presented with insufficient alternatives and uncertainty. V4 applies at moderate confidence; useful constraints retain counterfactual credit.

books.title: Travels in the Americas
books.author: Albert Camus
books.reason: These short journals preserve impressions and the author's state of mind. After removing travel encounters and personal observation, little sustained mechanism or general method remains for this task. Literary and historical value survive in the counterfactual score; V3 is about this payload test.

books.title: The Myth of Sisyphus
books.author: Albert Camus
books.reason: A philosophical argument about meaning and chosen action under an indifferent world provides durable practical concepts. Its reasoning is conceptual rather than an empirical mechanism, and technical fit is slight. It is an essay, so the myth in the title does not make the work fiction.

books.title: Une histoire populaire du baseball
books.author: Gaétan Alibert
books.reason: Biographical cases connect sport with exclusion, institutional change and social opportunity. Those links provide a modest payload, but baseball and social history remain far from the requested domains. The publisher's generic roman label conflicts with the described historical subject; retain as nonfiction provisionally.
books.identity: Author corrected to Gaétan Alibert. Historical subject matter supports provisional nonfiction classification; the publisher also uses a generic roman label, so genre confidence is low.

books.title: The Farfarers
books.author: Farley Mowat
books.reason: Brown's archaeological review identifies sound-alike place names and rejection of Dorset evidence as central defects in the proposed Alban migration history. Explicit speculation does not repair invalid inference from the available evidence. V1 applies; the book is marketed as historical nonfiction despite fictional reconstructions.

books.title: The DevOps Handbook
books.author: Gene Kim; Jez Humble; Patrick Debois; John Willis
books.reason: Flow, feedback, deployment and organizational learning connect software operations with management constraints. Case studies support practical methods but do not isolate each method's causal effect. Unlike The Phoenix Project, this is an expository handbook and passes the fiction gate.

books.title: Project Orion
books.author: George Dyson
books.reason: Propulsion physics, engineering scale, project organization and political constraints make an unusually strong technical history. The source's excitement about feasibility is not a completed safety or economic analysis. Historical optimism is examined as such rather than accepted as a current deployment plan.

books.title: The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up
books.author: Marie Kondo
books.reason: Categorization, reducing inventory and choosing what earns space provide simple reusable heuristics. Personal prescriptions and ritual framing are weak causal evidence, with little systems or technical relevance. Practical content survives the self-help packaging; no separate exclusion is permitted.

books.title: Why We Sleep
books.author: Matthew Walker
books.reason: The critique identifies overbroad risk statements and presentation problems. Walker's response qualifies cancer claims, promises corrections and distinguishes observational evidence from causality; it does not resolve every central overstatement. Retain real sleep science in the counterfactual while applying V1 at moderate confidence.

books.title: How to Do Nothing
books.author: Jenny Odell
books.reason: Attention, platforms, place and social incentives give a conceptual critique of productivity culture. The thread supplies specific objections about meandering exposition. Reflective utility remains, but evidence and density are limited, and ecology and place-based environmental attention are substantial organizing themes.

books.title: Flow
books.author: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
books.reason: Challenge, skill and feedback give a useful descriptive framework for absorbed work. Self-report and correlational evidence do not establish a universal recipe for flourishing. Research standing and durable concepts support inclusion; broad life advice reduces direct strategic fit.

books.title: Learned Optimism
books.author: Martin E. P. Seligman
books.reason: Explanatory style and learned helplessness connect experimental work to practical reframing. Animal-to-human and intervention generalization require limits; the source's personal improvement is not proof. Depression prevention and treatment are central enough for the deduction, while the reusable model prevents V3.

books.title: Anne Frank Remembered
books.author: Miep Gies; Alison Leslie Gold
books.reason: Concealment, resource scarcity, trust and institutional coercion emerge from firsthand testimony. These constraints give some transferable lessons, while the book remains a personal historical account rather than a causal study. Persecution is the predominant theme.

books.title: The Diary of a Young Girl
books.author: Anne Frank
books.reason: A contemporaneous diary records uncertainty, confinement and social relations under persecution. It provides a limited human-behavior payload, not a general survival mechanism. Textual and edition history matter; no supernatural or ideological veto follows from the author's identity.

books.title: Divine Proportions
books.author: Norman J. Wildberger
books.reason: Algebraic reformulation exposes exact invariants and computational possibilities in geometry. Correct results should be separated from claims that standard real analysis is illegitimate or that this approach is always superior. The narrow formal scope limits systems integration, while technical depth and durability are strong.

books.title: The 5 Elements of Effective Thinking
books.author: Edward B. Burger; Michael Starbird
books.reason: Testing simple cases, finding gaps and learning from errors give compact thinking procedures. The authors' mathematical practice supports authority, but anecdotes do not prove general performance gains. Excellent brevity and clarity coexist with familiar content and limited institutional depth.

books.title: Power vs. Force
books.author: David R. Hawkins
books.reason: The central method claims to calibrate truth and consciousness through muscle testing. Neither the procedure nor the numerical hierarchy provides a validated route to those conclusions; disagreement is explained through the same unverified hierarchy. V1 concerns the core epistemic method, not merely spiritual language.

books.title: Capital Is Dead
books.author: McKenzie Wark
books.reason: Ownership of information and control of networks provide a useful institutional lens. Treating these as a distinct post-capitalist mode is a contentious conceptual classification, not an established economic result. Weak operational tests lower evidence and precision; political theory still supplies some transferable questions.

books.title: The Immortality Key
books.author: Brian C. Muraresku
books.reason: Evidence for psychoactive substances in some ancient settings does not establish a continuous psychedelic origin of Greek mystery and Christian sacramental practice. Specialist criticism targets that central extrapolation. The archaeological search has documentary value, but V1 applies at moderate confidence to the proposed historical bridge.

books.title: Leonardo da Vinci
books.author: Walter Isaacson
books.reason: Observation, drawing, mechanics and cross-domain inquiry illuminate scientific and artistic practice. Extensive notebooks support the biography; extrapolated creativity lessons are less secure. The science and engineering biography exception applies, while large personal and art-historical sections reduce reading efficiency.

books.title: Cats’ Paws and Catapults
books.author: Steven Vogel
books.reason: Comparing natural and human devices exposes scaling, material limits, flow and design tradeoffs. Physical explanation and biological expertise make this highly reusable engineering intuition. It is biomechanical comparison, not predominantly ecology; many principles are familiar but their contrasting applications add value.

books.title: From Strength to Strength
books.author: Arthur C. Brooks
books.reason: Changing comparative advantage and choosing different aims with age offer useful reflection. Broad happiness and aging prescriptions rely heavily on selected lives and normative assumptions. The book is low priority for this reader, with enough practical ideas to prevent a no-payload veto.

books.title: The Fall of Rome and the End of Civilization
books.author: Bryan Ward-Perkins
books.reason: Material evidence for production, exchange and living standards tests claims of smooth transformation after Rome. The argument connects institutional breakdown to economic complexity. Regional variation and the catastrophe-versus-continuity framing require care, but the comparative civilizational payload is strong.

books.title: Cosmographia / A Description of Africa
books.author: Leo Africanus
books.reason: A historical geographical account gives direct evidence about routes, commerce and institutions as perceived by its author. Transmission, translation and selective observation limit reliability. Use it as a primary source with context, not as current geography or a comprehensive causal model.
books.identity: Leo Africanus’s own geographical work, not Amin Maalouf’s historical novel. Composed in the 1520s; first printed in 1550. Translation/volume unspecified.

books.title: Ways of Being
books.author: James Bridle
books.reason: Examples from computation and nonhuman cognition challenge narrow assumptions about intelligence. Analogies among organisms, algorithms and politics often outrun direct causal evidence. The central ecological and planetary program triggers the deduction; conceptual breadth does not validate every proposed equivalence.

books.title: EPA 608 Study Guide
books.author: Author unspecified
books.reason: The source supplies only EPA 608 Study Guide, without author, publisher, edition or link. Several different books use this title. No defensible whole-book criterion score or rating can be assigned to an unidentified text; retain the source record with NR rather than fabricate an assessment.
books.identity: Author, publisher and edition are not specified. A generic EPA 608 study-guide phrase does not identify a unique book. All criteria, year and rating remain NR.

books.title: Eichmann in Jerusalem
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.reason: The source interprets bureaucratic responsibility as a general mechanism. That does not resolve disputes over Eichmann's motives or validate a predictive formula for atrocity. Retain the earlier low-confidence vector, non-veto decision and deduction while separating philosophical utility from historical attribution.

books.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.reason: Ideology, terror, isolation and institutional destruction retain strong explanatory concepts. The historical chains need independent checking and the structure is demanding. The new comparison with Eichmann adds no reason to alter the earlier total or gate; systematic comparative politics is the main subject.

books.title: Russia: Revolution and Civil War, 1917–1921
books.author: Antony Beevor
books.reason: Command problems, coalition fragmentation and coercion help explain civil-war outcomes. Archival synthesis is strong, but narrative breadth exceeds mechanistic depth. Russia's revolution and civil war are the central national story, so the deduction applies despite foreign involvement.

books.title: Stalingrad
books.author: Antony Beevor
books.reason: Supply, geography, command incentives and morale explain a multinational campaign. The brief recommendation adds no new corroboration. Keep the complete prior vector and non-veto status; neither battle location nor brutality alone makes this single-nation or American-tragedy history.

books.title: Berlin: The Downfall 1945
books.author: Antony Beevor
books.reason: Operational constraints, competing command incentives and civilian collapse give a useful terminal-war case. The focus is narrower than the whole conflict, and source attribution needs care. A German-Soviet campaign with wider Allied context is not simply one nation's isolated history.

books.title: Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat
books.author: Samin Nosrat
books.reason: Four interacting cooking variables turn recipes into a useful constraint-based method. Testable practice and clear explanation earn evidence and mechanism points, although the technical domain is distant from the requested interests. Everyday utility prevents a low-fit exclusion.

books.title: Marx: A Very Short Introduction
books.author: Peter Singer; conditional identity
books.reason: If the source means Peter Singer's short introduction, it offers a compact critical map of Marx's arguments. It is not equivalent to endorsing Marx's conclusions or adding his books as new titles. Identity remains conditional because the comment gives a nonstandard series title and no author.
books.identity: Probable match to Peter Singer’s Marx (1980), repackaged as a Very Short Introduction in 2000. The source says very brief introduction and supplies no author.

books.title: Ace
books.author: Angela Chen
books.reason: Interviews and conceptual distinctions expose assumptions about desire, intimacy and social norms. They provide some reusable reasoning about categories, but not a general causal psychology. The minority-identity subject lowers fit, but is not itself a listed thematic deduction.

books.title: Complex PTSD: From Surviving to Thriving
books.author: Pete Walker
books.reason: The framework supplies coping exercises and a vocabulary for distress. Clinical experience and personal testimony do not validate every diagnostic category, memory claim or treatment mechanism. Retain provisionally with low evidence and utility; this review has not established a book-specific central flaw sufficient for a firm veto.

books.title: The Wizard and the Prophet
books.author: Charles C. Mann
books.reason: The source's reduced climate anxiety is a personal response, not new evidence. Competing models of technological expansion and ecological limits still connect research, production and institutions. Retain every earlier component and the environmental deduction; being a science biography does not waive T.

books.title: The Inner Game of Tennis
books.author: W. Timothy Gallwey
books.reason: Attention, feedback and reducing disruptive self-talk offer transferable performance heuristics. Coaching observations support practical authority but not a complete psychological mechanism. Sport is a poor fit, yet is not one of the listed automatic thematic deductions.

books.title: NeuroTribes
books.author: Steve Silberman
books.reason: Diagnostic categories, institutional incentives and changing research practice provide more than personal stories. Broad historical claims and selective cases require caution; the long narrative is not a technical account of cognition. The central disability and medical-social subject warrants the thematic cost.

books.title: Different Loving
books.author: Gloria G. Brame; William D. Brame; Jon Jacobs
books.reason: Interview-based description helps distinguish consent, social norms and community practices. Sampling limits prevent population-wide conclusions and the historical snapshot is dated. Some social mechanisms survive, but the minority-sexuality focus and weak direct fit make priority very low.

books.title: Walking Your Blues Away
books.author: Thom Hartmann
books.reason: The book turns a proposed link between walking, bilateral stimulation and emotional recovery into a therapeutic method without adequate support for that causal bridge. General benefits of walking or evidence for clinician-delivered EMDR do not validate the specific method. V1 is a moderate-confidence judgment.

books.title: The Soul of a New Machine
books.author: Tracy Kidder
books.reason: Design constraints, deadlines, tacit knowledge and team incentives make engineering work visible. Close observation and strong narrative support evidence and clarity; one project cannot establish universal management rules. Durable organizational lessons remain after the original hardware is obsolete.

books.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
books.author: Martin Kleppmann
books.reason: Replication, consistency, storage and distributed failure are explained through tradeoffs and explicit models. Technical depth, source references and architecture make the work highly reusable. The 2017 edition is the source-nominated work; later technology changes do not erase its core constraints.

books.title: Recoding America
books.author: Jennifer Pahlka
books.reason: Policy implementation, feedback and service design show how good intentions fail in delivery. Practitioner access gives concrete organizational lessons, but US-specific rules limit transfer. The subject is directly useful for technology and institutions while still predominantly American domestic administration.

books.title: Quantum Electrodynamics
books.author: Richard P. Feynman; conditional edition
books.reason: On the literal identification, these are Feynman's technical lectures, with precise amplitudes and calculational methods. They are durable and concise, although a QFT specialist gains less novelty. The comment's accessible description could instead mean QED (1985); this score is conditional on the 1961 title.
books.identity: Literal match: Feynman’s Quantum Electrodynamics (1961). The comment’s short, accessible description may mean QED: The Strange Theory of Light and Matter (1985). The numerical assessment is conditional on the literal technical title; do not transfer it to the popular book.

books.title: The Jakarta Method
books.author: Vincent Bevins
books.reason: The account connects anti-communist violence, international intervention and institutional power across countries. Strong reporting supports the cases; selection and causal attribution remain the main limits. The new source adds no independent corrective evidence, so retain the prior vector and low confidence.

books.title: Poverty, by America
books.author: Matthew Desmond
books.reason: The book identifies incentives that sustain poverty, while policy selection and causal emphasis remain contestable. Its institutional mechanisms survive beyond the American cases, but the predominant US domestic subject warrants T. The new mention does not justify changing any earlier component.

books.title: Evicted
books.author: Matthew Desmond
books.reason: Close fieldwork links housing insecurity, landlord incentives, courts and household choices. The evidence is rich but local and observational. Retain the previous assessment and deduction: the new comment supplies no basis for changing the generalization limits or the strong case-level evidence.

books.title: README.txt
books.author: Chelsea Manning
books.reason: A participant account can illuminate military information systems, secrecy and institutional treatment, but personal testimony needs external checks. Identity, imprisonment and US politics dominate. Some mechanisms remain, so weak fit does not itself justify V3.

books.title: What's Our Problem?
books.author: Tim Urban
books.reason: The contrast between open inquiry and group allegiance offers usable prompts, but large social categories and selected political examples outrun systematic evidence. Length and repetition weaken density. Current US polarization limits durability; the source is insufficient to establish a serious veto.

books.title: The Story of Art Without Men
books.author: Katy Hessel
books.reason: An alternative art survey changes which work is visible and gives useful examples of institutional selection. Its main payload remains art history rather than system mechanisms. Women's art history is not automatically one of the specified thematic categories; do not manufacture a deduction.

books.title: Uproar!
books.author: Alice Loxton
books.reason: Print technology, satire and public reputation connect art with political communication. Biographical episodes carry some transferable insight, but Georgian Britain is the main historical frame. The national-history deduction applies; neither political subject matter nor lively prose alone implies capture.

books.title: Thinking in Systems
books.author: Donella H. Meadows
books.reason: Stocks, flows, delays, feedback and intervention points provide compact, reusable causal tools. Examples explain failure modes without making every system predictable. Some ecological examples occur, but the book's principal payload is a general method, so the environmental deduction does not apply.

books.title: The Body: A Guide for Occupants
books.author: Bill Bryson
books.reason: A clear anatomical tour provides many facts and some functional explanations. Anecdotes and breadth exceed mechanistic depth; it is not a technical physiology text. Disease is one component of a whole-body survey, not clearly its predominant subject, so T is not applied.

books.title: The Song of the Cell
