books.author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
books.reason: Cell biology is connected to clinical practice and historical discovery with strong medical authority. The explanatory material survives the patient stories, but medical failure and treatment occupy enough of the narrative to warrant the disease deduction. Specialist cellular detail is selective.

books.title: Lexicon Urthus
books.author: Michael Andre-Driussi
books.reason: This is a nonfiction reference companion to Gene Wolfe's fictional world, not itself a novel. Its entries may serve readers well, but names, fictional geography and textual cross-references supply almost all its value. Removing that local detail leaves insufficient transferable payload for this profile.

books.title: Don't Think of an Elephant!
books.author: George Lakoff
books.reason: Framing and metaphor explain part of political persuasion, but the explicit partisan purpose selects examples and advice. Useful linguistic mechanisms remain. Advocacy alone does not establish V2; the limited causal evidence and American political focus already constrain the score.

books.title: Nicomachean Ethics
books.author: Aristotle; probable identity
books.reason: Practical judgment, habituation and distinctions between ends supply durable ethical tools. This is a normative argument, not an empirical psychology textbook; ancient social assumptions need separation from valid reasoning. Translation and the source's unspecific reference to Aristotle make identity and prose scores conditional.
books.identity: Probable identification of the source’s Aristotle ethics reference; exact translation unspecified. The assessment concerns the philosophical work, not a specific translator.

books.title: Republic
books.author: Plato
books.reason: The dialogue links education, incentives, justice and political order through explicit arguments. Several institutional proposals and psychological analogies are weak, but the work remains useful for testing premises rather than following a program. Philosophical dialogue is treated as nonfiction, with translation uncertainty.

books.title: Excellent Sheep
books.author: William Deresiewicz
books.reason: Selection incentives and prestige competition provide a plausible institutional critique. Essays and personal observation do not establish all claims about elite students or alternatives. US higher education dominates; the argument retains some transfer but needs independent evidence before policy use.

books.title: Airborne Electronic Hardware Design Assurance
books.author: Randall Fulton; Roy Vandermolen
books.reason: Hardware assurance links requirements, verification, traceability and certification constraints in a safety-critical setting. The narrow technical procedure is relevant to engineering risk, though much administration and standard-specific detail limit general use. A 2014 manual must be checked against the governing standard for any live project.
books.identity: Early release records point to 2014, while copyright/catalogue records also give 2015. Edition uncertainty is retained.

books.title: God: A Human History
books.author: Reza Aslan
books.reason: The history proposes psychological mechanisms for making gods human-like. Its broad cross-cultural narrative exceeds the evidence for a single explanation of religion. Competing interpretations limit confidence, but neither the source nor checked descriptions establish a sufficiently serious central error for V1.

books.title: Zealot
books.author: Reza Aslan
books.reason: Political context helps explain religious authority and conflict, but reconstructing a historical individual from sparse, contested sources involves large inference. The bold thesis should not be treated as scholarly consensus. Retain with low confidence rather than equating disagreement or religious subject matter with a veto.

books.title: No god but God
books.author: Reza Aslan
books.reason: Religious interpretation, institutions and political authority are linked across Islamic history. The readable synthesis has a reformist perspective and compresses scholarly disputes; it is not a neutral exhaustive reference. Transferable institutional mechanisms remain and no serious veto is sufficiently established.

books.title: The Rise and Fall of Ancient Egypt
books.author: Toby Wilkinson
books.reason: State formation, resource control, coercion and legitimacy emerge through a long chronology. Broad synthesis supplies context but many royal episodes have limited transfer. The scope is predominantly one civilization, so the single-nation-history deduction is applied even though modern nationhood is an imperfect analogy.

books.title: The Long Game
books.author: Dorie Clark; probable identity
books.reason: Long horizons, selective commitments and delayed rewards are sensible planning heuristics. Coaching examples offer limited tests and substantial material is familiar. Identity is conditional because the source gives no author; a low score and self-help genre are not extra exclusion rules.
books.identity: Probable Dorie Clark identification; the comment gives only The Long Game.

books.title: Charlie Munger: The Complete Investor
books.author: Tren Griffin; probable identity
books.reason: Mental models, incentives and avoiding investment errors are useful across decisions. A synthesis of a successful investor's remarks has selection and survivorship limits and is not a validated strategy. The source's shortened title makes identification with Griffin conditional.
books.identity: Probable match to Tren Griffin’s Charlie Munger: The Complete Investor; the source shortens the title.

books.title: The Language of Emotions
books.author: Karla McLaren
books.reason: Distinguishing emotions and reflecting before acting can be useful, but assigning stable messages to each emotion risks false precision. The framework is more a practitioner interpretation than tested causal theory. Retain with low confidence because specific serious central failure has not been established.

books.title: Taking the Work Out of Networking
books.author: Karen Wickre
books.reason: Maintaining relationships through small regular actions is practical and transferable. Personal experience gives examples rather than causal evidence; much advice is common sense. Networking is not the desired domain, but that is scored as fit and does not justify exclusion.

books.title: Lessons in Stoicism
books.author: John Sellars
books.reason: A short scholarly introduction makes control, judgment and attention usable without a long self-help narrative. It explains selected Stoic ideas rather than testing a complete psychology. The compact form earns density while limited system integration and direct domain fit keep priority moderate.

books.title: Man's Search for Meaning
books.author: Viktor E. Frankl
books.reason: The source adds a personal endorsement, not independent support for the therapeutic generalizations. Distinguish the testimony's historical value from the thinner causal case for meaning as treatment. Retain all prior components, including the Holocaust-focused racial-persecution deduction.

books.title: Americana
books.author: Bhu Srinivasan
books.reason: Business episodes connect infrastructure, technology, capital and consumer demand across American development. Broad scope and strong mechanisms help, while selective success stories and length constrain inference and density. The US focus remains predominant despite the general lessons.

books.title: Program = Proof
books.author: Samuel Mimram
books.reason: Constructive logic, typed programs and proof techniques connect formal claims to executable structure. Precise definitions and exercises make the knowledge reusable for a mathematically trained reader. Narrow social integration is a scope limit, while the technical payload and durability are high.
books.identity: The paperback has a 979 ISBN; the author’s bibliographic record also gives ASIN B08C97TD9G.

books.title: Rust Atomics and Locks
books.author: Mara Bos
books.reason: Memory ordering, synchronization and low-level primitives are explained through explicit constraints and examples. The result is directly useful for numerical and systems programming. Language-specific details can age, while the reasoning about concurrency remains durable.
books.identity: The author dates the book January 2023; some retailer records use late 2022 release metadata. Use the author’s publication year.

books.title: Statistical Consequences of Fat Tails
books.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
books.reason: Heavy tails, pre-asymptotic behavior and estimation error expose practical failure modes in risk models. Technical derivations give substantially more payload than slogans; broad real-world extrapolations still need checking. Uneven exposition and some argumentative excess limit clarity and precision.

books.title: The Golden Rules
books.author: Bob Bowman; Charles Butler
books.reason: Elite coaching experience yields discipline and feedback routines, but selection effects prevent strong causal claims about success. Familiar motivational advice supplies modest transfer outside sport. Sports and self-help are low fit, not formal thematic deduction categories or automatic vetoes.

books.title: Down and Out in Paris and London
books.author: George Orwell
books.reason: Firsthand experience makes labor insecurity and social status concrete, though reconstructed scenes and a small personal sample limit inference. Observations have transferable institutional value, so the book passes V3. Poverty and urban life are the predominant subject and incur T.

books.title: The Bible
books.author: Multiple ancient authors
books.reason: A diverse religious and literary collection has no single empirical central argument. Earlier V1 reasoning treated it as a factual explanatory authority; this source uses it as a comparison and does not support that assumption. Remove the blanket veto, retain weak empirical reliability and low domain fit; no endorsement of supernatural claims follows.
books.identity: No canon, translation or single publication year is specified. The centuries shown describe the main textual formation, not one dated edition. No reader score is assigned to the unspecified collection.

books.title: Stolen Focus
books.author: Johann Hari
books.reason: Attention is connected to business incentives, work conditions and personal behavior, yielding some reusable mechanisms. Journalistic case selection and simplified causal claims limit reliability; personal experiments do not isolate causes. Retain cautiously because the source supplies no decisive evidence of a serious central failure.

books.title: A Path Through the Jungle
books.author: Steve Peters
books.reason: A structured practice program offers tools for habits, emotional control and resilience. Its simplified brain model is a teaching metaphor, not a literal account of neural organization; causal evidence for the complete program is limited. Generic self-help is low fit but not an automatic exclusion.

books.title: Sacred Economics
books.author: Charles Eisenstein
books.reason: Debt, interest, commons and gift exchange provide some institutional questions. A normative vision and broad claims about money and social separation exceed the historical and economic evidence; proposed reforms need independent testing. Ecological restoration is central. Retain at low confidence rather than treat an unconventional outlook alone as a veto.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.author: Stuart Russell; Peter Norvig
books.reason: Search, inference, planning, learning and decisions under uncertainty connect formal methods with working algorithms. Textbook breadth, references and exercises make the mechanisms testable. The source specifies the fourth edition; fast-moving neural applications need current supplements, while the core models remain durable and directly useful.
books.identity: First edition 1995 according to the authors’ edition history; source specifies fourth edition, issued in 2020 (global paperback 2021).

books.title: In Defense of Civilization
books.author: Michael R. J. Bonner
books.reason: Historical comparisons connect cultural memory, institutions and recovery after collapse. They suggest useful constraints but do not establish a general law of renewal or prove a modern prescription. Normative selection and a broad civilizational frame limit evidence; the available material does not establish a serious ideological veto.
